title: Grateful Dead Live at Greek Theatre, U. Of California on 1982-05-22
lineage: Sbd Mcassette > DAT > CDR > CDR >  EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Scorching early‑80s Greek show captured on a crisp soundboard tape; first‑set fires with Jack Straw → Sugaree and the iconic Lazy Lightning > Supplication, while the second set delivers blazing China‑Rider and a standout Not Fade Away jam.
ai_review.review: The performance is consistently high‑energy, with reviewers calling the entire first set “smoking” and highlighting tight renditions of Jack Straw, Sugaree, Lazy Lightning > Supplication, and Deal. The second half shines thanks to an inspiring China Cat/Rider transition, a powerful Not Fade Away jam, and Brent’s soulful Good Times Blues (Never Trust A Woman). The soundboard source is praised as clear and crisp, with only minor tape‑hiss or level fluctuations noted.

ai_rating.rationale: Over 30 detailed reviews overwhelmingly rate the show 4–5 stars and praise both musical performance and sound quality; only a few low‑rating outliers exist, so the combined weighted rating is strongly positive.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clear mix with strong instrument separation; occasional tape hiss and minor level fluctuations (vocals sometimes louder/softer), but overall very listenable.

standout_songs: Never Trust a Woman (Women Are Smarter)
Good Times Blues (aka Never Trust A Woman)
show_quality.setlist_flow: A high‑octane opening first set that maintains momentum into a second set packed with tight jams and seamless transitions, especially the China‑Rider/NFA sequence.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Vocals described as strong, clear and possibly his best of the early ’80s; guitar tone noted as solid.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass is “very clear in the mix,” with listeners appreciating his presence throughout.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir’s vocals are generally praised (especially on Deal and later songs); occasional mention of a penny‑whistle embellishment during Space.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland highlighted for soulful vocal on Good Times Blues, reverb‑enhanced delivery, and tight interplay with Jerry; no specific comments on Keith or Vince.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming called tight and supportive of the band’s high energy; no major issues reported.
